mrsnotredamegarde.name: Notre-Dame de la Garde
mrsnotredamegarde.slogan: La Bonne Mère, gold-leafed and watching every ship in.
mrsnotredamegarde.line: Marseillais call it La Bonne Mère; the gilded Virgin on its bell tower stands 11.2 metres tall.

mrschateauif.name: Château d'If
mrschateauif.slogan: A tiny island fortress that made a fictional count famous.
mrschateauif.line: Built by Francis I between 1524 and 1531, it held 3,500 Huguenots, yet no real prisoner is known to have escaped.

arlesamphitheatre.name: Arles Amphitheatre
arlesamphitheatre.slogan: Roman arches that once sheltered a whole village.
arlesamphitheatre.line: Built around 90 AD with 120 arches, it later held over 200 houses and two chapels inside its walls.

bauxchateau.name: Château des Baux
bauxchateau.slogan: A ruined fortress on a cliff where bauxite got its name.
bauxchateau.line: Bauxite is named after this village, where geologist Pierre Berthier found the ore in the 1820s.

aixcoursmirabeau.name: Cours Mirabeau
aixcoursmirabeau.slogan: Plane trees, mossy fountains and Aix's longest-running people-watching.
aixcoursmirabeau.line: Laid out in 1650 on a crumbled rampart, this 440 m avenue was a haunt of Cézanne and Zola.
